copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Norway v Senegal in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Tuesday, and the model and the market disagree on the Senegal side by +14.5pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

The Elo prior reads Norway 1760 vs Senegal 1790: 30 points in favour of Senegal, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Norway to win at 33%, the draw at 28%, and Senegal to win at 39%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Senegal on the win side reads 39%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Norway to win at 50%, the draw at 24%, and Senegal to win at 24%. Polymarket has Senegal at 24%, which prices out at American odds of +308; the model has the same side at 39%. The +14.5pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Senegal, that haircut lands the model at 32%; the market is at 24%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +7.3pp. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Senegal side.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 34 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Senegal a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +14.5pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +14.5pp gap across model and market on the Senegal side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Senegal at 39%; Polymarket sits at 24%.
copy.title: Norway v Senegal · the model leans Senegal
